chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Leaving Tulsa a month before graduation; a hernia
summary: He clarifies leaving Tulsa and graduating at Jefferson, and describes a hernia.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: The story you told about your high school graduation and the white shoes you didn't have, you didn't place it in Los Angeles. Because we were talking there and you jumped from some high school experiences in Tulsa to graduation, but you -- I wanted to make it absolutely clear.
I left Tulsa a month before graduation. I left Tulsa a month before graduation.
And then you graduated from Jefferson High School in Los Angeles.
You told me off the tape about joining the band at Jefferson. Could you tell me on the tape?
Oh, yeah. Did I tell you on the tape.
No. Not about the Jefferson band. You mentioned joining the band but that's all you said on the tape.

Oh. Well, as I didn't have to attend any classes, I wanted to be around the music, you know. And in spite of having to have this operation and this scar tissue, when I first started back to school, I picked up my horn too

soon, and busted the incision from the inside, which caused a small hernia. And I had three operations in the same spot. And it remained a hernia. And I was supposed to go back to the hospital and have it straightened out. They let me out to gain some strength and get some sunshine and come back. I went back. They said, 'Is it bothering you?' I said, 'No.' They said, 'Well, leave it alone. Don't trouble it until it troubles you,' you know. Say, 'You might live to be a ripe old age with it, and never bother you,' you know.
And the scar tissue has never broken open, you know, like from the outside. 'So, you're in no danger, you know. You can live with it.' So I never did go back to have it straightened out. You know.
Now, what were we talking about before that?
